This sung-through musical is rousing entertainment for all of its nearly 'three hours straight,' and much of the delight comes from seeing how Taub manipulates the material to make it fun.

Just as the suffragists broke down the doors of the patriarchy, Suffs breaks down the doors of musical theatre, showing that a cast and creative team of mostly women can tell a story that is important, powerful, and about all of us.

Leaning heavily on rhetorical flourishes, Taub's score is filled with lots of well-meaning exhortations to 'finish the fight,' earnest appeals that quickly lose emotional resonance through a lack of lyrical variance and depth.
Suffs isn't as miserable an experience as it might read under analysis but...it isn't a drum worth beating.

It is a tribute to director Leigh Silverman along with musical supervisor Andrea Grody and choreographer and creative consultant Raja Feather Kelly that they have helped to create a world where all aspects of Taub’s creativity shines.

Shaina Taub has spent eight years researching and condensing the adventures of women’s rights activist Alice Paul and her cronies into a manageable tale. Despite the comparatively concise final product, at nearly three hours in runtime, Suffs (shorthand for women who fought to win the right to vote) still feels too long to absorb in one sitting.
